[City of Pearl, Center.]

Granting an uninhibited view of the bustling shipping industry, a stone seawall bevels out behind a long crescent bench and creates a half-moon addition to the congested crossroads at the heart of the city.  The vast water of the bay expands beyond the southern stone wall.  Ships of all sizes pass by the seafront as they make their way in and out of the harbor to the south.  The streets head in many directions, as well as a tunnel to the northeast.  At the center of the intersection is an elegantly carved monument of a giant pearl atop a tall obelisk.  The base of the centerpiece rests at the bottom of a shallow fountain that has a burning spear pointing down into the water.  A small stone sundial has been carved on the rim of the fountain.  You notice a wooden directional signpost.

Obvious Exits: southwest, southeast, northwest, northeast, west, east, and north.

[Lunstin Pass.]

The southeastern path leading away from the cobblestone streets of the academy are all but overgrown from years of neglect.  The path was originally cleared to provide access to the nearby forest when the academy was being built, but rumors of a haunted forest have all but halted the forestry industry.  Only adventurers now travel to what the locals refer to as the "Tallwood Forest."

help follow

Command : FOLLOW
Usage   : FOLLOW [CHARACTER NAME]
Example : follow Poiuy
Short(s): fol
In order to form adventuring groups, one or more characters may choose to follow another player.  That character then becomes the group leader, and is able to lead his or her followers around the map without their intervention.

Followers may walk away from the group at any time by moving in any direction, however, they still remain part of the group until they LEAVE or the leader removes them with LOSE [PLAYER].  If neither happens and they reunite with the group, they will automatically travel with them once again.  The number of followers a leader may have depends upon his or her Charisma stat.

Use LEAVE to stop following in a group.
To force a follower to stop following you, use LOSE [PLAYER NAME].

See the GROUP, LOSE, DIAGNOSE, and SPLIT commands for more information.

[Summoner Street, Main Gate.]

The cobblestones along this end of the street do not show nearly as much wear as the ones further north near the market square.  Those traveling this far south are generally heading to, or back from, an adventure outside the protection of the academy walls to test their skills in combat.  A wrought iron lantern casts an illuminating glow over the street.  A towering stone wall extends in opposite directions from a heavy steel gate with thick steel bars making up its width. You notice an open large steel gate, and a weathered wooden sign with the word "WARNING" boldly engraved.

[Southland Intersection.]

A tall, white tower can be seen in the northern sky.  You notice an open intricately detailed iron gate, and a wooden directional signpost.

se



[Lunstin Pass.]

The path was originally cleared to provide access to the nearby forest when the academy was being built, but rumors of a haunted forest have all but halted the forestry industry.  Only adventurers now travel to what the locals refer to as the "Tallwood Forest."

A transcribed recipe reads, "
___________________________________________________________

Students of the Academy,
Students of the Academy, Welcome to New Archai.
What follows is a series of recipes and information meant to guide you into the world of the culinary arts, or for those less inclined to such pursuits - a way to feed yourselves at least.

Key ingredients that will benefit you in your early cooking are:

1) Salt
2) Meat
3) Herbs
4) Water
5) A foraged vegetable such as turnips, potatoes, carrots, corn.

**Author's Note: You may wish to store bundles of these ingredients in the depository to keep them from spoiling. Packets of 25, 50 or 100 make for ease of use when learning how to cook.

----Three Chapters of Cuisine, a Beginner's Guide to Pearlean Gastronomy----
By Emissary Faran Fairuz-Taqqi, Khalsat of Kaleith

**Author's Note: Salt is easily found by mining in the Orc Caves of the academy, located to the west outside of the south gate up along the Highland Road. Meat, and other bits,  can be skinned from the animals residing in the Tallwood Forest, located south and east outside of the south gate. Vegetables, herbs, rice and other accoutrements may be foraged in the Tallwood as well, or likewise foraged in the farmlands to the northeast of the woods.

----Chapter 1----

1.Butter
**Author’s Note: Useful in a number of advanced recipes, butter will become a staple in the more accessible cuisine of boiled corn, scrambled eggs and sauteed mushrooms.
To prepare: Mix 10 cups water, 1 cup milk and 1 pinch of salt into a pot, bring to boil and then let rest.

2. Boiled potatoes
To prepare: Mix 10 cups water, 1 pound potatoes and 1 spring herbs in a pot.

3. Boiled carrots
To prepare: Boil 1 pound carrots in 10 cups of water with 1 spring of herbs.

4. Boiled turnips
To prepare: Boil 1 cup turnips in 10 cups of water with 1 sprig of herbs.

5.Cooked Beans
To prepare: Boil 1 cup beans with 1 pinch of salt in 10 cups of water.

6. Hardboiled egg
**Author's Note: Eggs can be purchased from the Butcher's Daughter in Hawker's Alley of the Academy, or coerced from chickens in the farmlands of Dalarey in Pearl.
To prepare: Boil 1 egg with 1 pinch of salt in 10 cups of water.

7. Boiled meat
**Author's Note: This recipe is one of the easiest to make, given its ingredients, and will aid in learning advanced techniques.
To prepare: Boil 1 pound meat with 1 pinch of salt in 10 cups of water.

8. Rabbit stew
To prepare: Slow cook 1 cup of rabbit meat with 1 cup of potatoes and 1 pinch of salt in 10 cups of water.

----Chapter 2----

9. Boiled corn
To prepare: Boil 1 ear of corn in 10 cups of water, adding 1 stick of butter for flavor.

10. Vegetable soup
To prepare: Slow cook 1 cup of carrots, 1 cup of potatoes and 1 cup of corn in 10 cups of water.

11. Boiled rice
**Authors Note: Another easy and quick recipe, due to the abudance of forageable salt and rice in the Academy.
To prepare: Boil 1 cup rice with 1 pinch of salt in 10 cups of water.

----Chapter 3----

12. Scrambled eggs
To prepare: Fry 2 eggs with 1 tablespoon of butter and 1 pinch of salt.
**Author's Note: Remember to EMPTY your pot of water before placing your ingredients in to cook. You can FILL your pot from a water source (Shattered Lake, wells, fountains and even your waterskin at a later time).

13. Boiled quail
To prepare: Poach 1 quail breast in 10 cups of water, adding 1 sprig of herbs for aromatics and flavor.

14. Boiled chicken
To prepare: Poach 1 breast of chicken in 10 cups of water, adding 1 sprig of herbs for aromatics and flavor.

15. Beef stew
To prepare: Slow cook 1 pound of meat in 10 cups of water with 1 cup of carrots, 1 cup of potatoes, 1 cup corn and 1 cup of tomatoes for a hearty, robust meal.

Have fun exploring the many locales around you to forage, dig, and collect useful ingredients for your culinary adventure.

Fair tides and majestic mastication,
~Faran


___________________________________________________________
"

[Hawkers' Alley, Entrance.]

A large faded banner rises up above a dun colored cloth canopy that does little to provide shelter from the elements.  Once sturdy and brightly colored, it now hangs in tatters in some places and worn to the point of translucency in others.

[Hawkers Alley.]

Dust hangs heavy in the air, kicked up by the foot traffic of crafters coming and going in a steady stream.  Chefs and their apprentices cluster around the produce stand and meat market to the northeast and southwest respectively.  Vendors call out their special items to attract attention as aspiring cooks search for ingredients of special recipes.  Saw and stone dust-covered craftsmen continue farther down the alley, looking for their own wares.

A large marble fountain anchors the central crossroads of the academy, right at the heart of the marketplace.  Rainbow mists float through the air, reflecting any available light.  Smooth, white stone neatly paves the circular roadway encompassing the fountain.  To the north, a looming stone structure rises above the cityscape in grandiose form.  Constant traffic of locals and adventurers heading toward the north lends to the building's purpose as the academy school, while many others take advantage of the services available nearby. [City of Pearl, Center.]

Granting an uninhibited view of the bustling shipping industry, a stone seawall bevels out behind a long crescent bench and creates a half-moon addition to the congested crossroads at the heart of the city.  The vast water of the bay expands beyond the southern stone wall.  Ships of all sizes pass by the seafront as they make their way in and out of the harbor to the south.  The streets head in many directions, as well as a tunnel to the northeast.  At the center of the intersection is an elegantly carved monument of a giant pearl atop a tall obelisk.  The base of the centerpiece rests at the bottom of a shallow fountain that has a burning spear pointing down into the water.  A small stone sundial has been carved on the rim of the fountain.  You notice a wooden directional signpost.

Also here: a navy blue-robed constable, a portly town crier, and a navy blue-robed constable

     After a long battle, recent reports of the plague indicate its grasp 
on New Archai has diminished.  In anticipation of the Pearlean King's orders 
to bring guards back home from the outskirts, some adventurers have begun 
organizing expeditions into plague-infested areas to eradicate any lingering 
signs of the illness.  Traveling outside of New Archai Isle remains diffi-
cult as tensions at sea have escalated between the Archai Trading Company, 
supported by the King's royal fleet, and the Kalesian-led navy whom aim to 
cut off key trade routes.

     After more than two centuries, rumors swirl of the return of wyverns 
and dragons.  Piercing screeches in the night followed by bellowing roars 
do nothing to dispel the rumors as myth.  Sightings had been reported all 
over the isle, though with little evidence to back any of the claims until 
a charred, winged figure came crashing down in King's Port.  Though mangled, 
the remains were believed to be that of a wyvern.  Meanwhile, political tur-
moil between conclave and crown has reached a boiling point with conclave 
passing law after law in an effort to hold the royal Knight Marshals 
accountable for their actions.
